verdict.rationale: Worker-loss tolerance is documented: Conductor detects when an executor disconnects or crashes and recovers the workflow onto another healthy executor (dbos-docs-31), and checkpointing lets work resume without re-running completed steps (dbos-docs-36, dbos-docs-4). Postgres-backed queues provide managed concurrency (dbos-docs-6), and a distributing-agents guide exists, but the evidence never explicitly says tasks are load-balanced across a fleet or that throughput scales linearly as workers are added. A community critique raises worker contention and global rate-limit coordination as concerns (dbos-comm-6), but that is skepticism, not a demonstrated failure. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of distributing queue tasks across multiple workers, evidence of horizontal throughput scaling, cross-executor recovery without Conductor, independent scale benchmarks.
